coursesExamined.name: Personal & Professional Development
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
coursesExamined.contribution: RequiredPPDacademic/civicformation.
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

coursesExamined.name: Optimization Methods in AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies search and optimization for rational agents in known, complex and adversarial environments. Students move from uninformed and heuristic search to local and global optimization, first- and second-order methods and population approaches. Adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimization extend the toolkit. Laboratories and projects require algorithm tracing, implementation and evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops computational search and constraint satisfaction for the evidenced biological-modelling direction, complementing numerical and algebraic model-solving methods; it is not a molecular-simulation or biophysics course
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and heuristic search, local and global optimisation, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation. Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.

coursesExamined.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies algorithm design and analysis, emphasizing how algorithms and data structures affect execution time. Students examine sorting, searching, random-number generation, string matching and graph algorithms, then study computability, verification, reductions and complexity classes. Programming and mathematical exercises develop algorithmic understanding, while projects require students to design, execute and report experimental investigations of performance.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis for computational biological data/model workflows; biological sequence-analysis content is not invented
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Teaches design and analysis of algorithms and data structures, emphasizing performance analysis and focusing on prominent algorithms and data structures.

coursesExamined.name: Advanced Algorithms
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies algebraic algorithms and advanced optimization methods through mathematical reasoning, implementation and experimental analysis. Fast and exact arithmetic, number-theoretic algorithms, matrix multiplication and Fourier transformation lead into hashing, greedy methods, dynamic programming and network flows. Laboratories develop algorithmic understanding, while projects investigate exact computing and optimization, including hypotheses, measured performance and sensitivity analysis.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops algebraic algorithms, optimisation and mathematical modelling, extending the algorithmic tools available for the target’s quantitative/computational science direction
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Studies modern algebraic algorithms and optimization methods. Emphasises algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling of computational problems.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Data Science
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data. Students import, clean, transform and join data, explore patterns, and construct visualizations using tidy-data principles and the grammar of graphics. Web scraping and basic programming functions extend the workflow. A student research project applies these tools to a question using data from a field of interest.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation for interpreting biological measurements; disciplinary examples do not imply dedicated genomics training
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.

coursesExamined.name: Machine Learning
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes. Students study regression and classification, model accuracy, resampling, regularization, nonlinear models, trees, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Practical assignments evaluate methods on real data using R or Python. Projects emphasize informative predictor construction, test-set prediction, appropriate model choice and clear reporting of results and limitations.
coursesExamined.contribution: Regression/classification,resampling,regularisation,trees,SVM andunsupervisedlearning withrealdata projects support empirical biological modelling. No guaranteedmedical dataset or specialistbiological course claimed.
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.

coursesExamined.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognize structures and objects. Spatial and spectral representations, colour and image statistics support filtering, segmentation, curve and feature detection, tracking and object classification. Students use Python and OpenCV to implement image-processing techniques, investigate spectral representations, and build a recognition pipeline whose performance is benchmarked on previously unseen images.
coursesExamined.contribution: Digitalimage representation,spatial/spectral analysis,filtering,segmentation,features/tracking/classification andPython/OpenCVrecognitionpipeline supply concrete quantitative imageanalysis methods. Opticalacquisition,nanoscopy or guaranteedmedicalimages are notclaimed.
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognise structures and objects. Topics include colour, image statistics, filtering, segmentation, feature detection, tracking and object classification. Practical work uses Python and OpenCV to develop and benchmark an image-recognition pipeline on previously unseen images.

coursesExamined.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops neural-network theory and practical implementation in Python, Keras and TensorFlow. Students build and train simple networks before studying multilayer architectures, backpropagation, regularization and model evaluation. Later work applies deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects construct predictors for tabular data and investigate an independently chosen image- or text-based prediction problem, with experimental results reported in a paper.
coursesExamined.contribution: implements artificial neural networks and computer-vision models, supporting computational analysis and the selected neural-network elective connection; artificial networks do not replace biological neurophysiology
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python, Keras and TensorFlow implementations. Students build and train networks, study backpropagation, regularisation and model evaluation, and apply deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects investigate prediction problems and report experimental results.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Programming
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces computational problem-solving and programming in Python. Students develop structured programs using branching, iteration, functions and data collections, then progress to recursion, exception handling and object-oriented programming with inheritance. Elements of logic, sets and enumeration support computational reasoning. Exercises and projects require students to write, trace, test, debug and explain programs that solve problems of moderate complexity.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops programming, testing and computational problem-solving as the foundation for the target’s scientific-programming and biological-analysis work
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.

coursesExamined.name: Mathematical Methods
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops single-variable calculus and related mathematical tools for modelling scientific problems. Functions, limits and differentiation lead to optimization, Taylor series, complex numbers, integration and differential equations. Students solve problems analytically and with Mathematica, including numerical approximation. A project implements, analyzes and adapts a dynamic model, requiring interpretation of its behaviour and explanation of the computational results.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops calculus,complexnumbers,integration,differentialequations anddynamicmodel implementation/analysis withMathematica. These are specificmathematicalmethod foundations; vectors/matrix/eigenvalueclaims belong toLinearAlgebra,not thiscourse.
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. Students solve problems analytically and with Mathematica. A project implements, analyses and adapts a dynamic model, requiring interpretation of its behaviour and computational results.

coursesExamined.name: Linear Algebra
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops linear algebra from systems of equations and matrix operations to vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and orthogonality. Students study least-squares approximation, symmetric matrices, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis. Mathematica exercises teach computer-algebra approaches to larger problems alongside analytical problem-solving.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops matrix methods and linear spaces for representing interacting biological variables and computational models
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Linear Algebra studies systems of equations, matrices, vectors, linear transformations and vector spaces. Students examine eigenvalues, orthogonality, least-squares approximation, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis, with Mathematica supporting analytical problem-solving.

coursesExamined.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops numerical solutions to mathematical problems that lack convenient analytical solutions, emphasizing when algorithms work and how to validate their output. Students study numerical root finding, interpolation, differentiation, quadrature, ordinary differential equations, and linear and nonlinear systems. Mathematica notebooks apply and compare textbook algorithms with built-in routines, with attention to roundoff, convergence, error, stability and sensitivity.
coursesExamined.contribution: implements numerical equation solving, integration and differential equations, supplying the actual computational methods for dynamic biological models
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Introduces numerical methods such as root‑finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration and solving differential equations. Emphasises algorithm accuracy, stability and efficiency and uses computer algebra software.

coursesExamined.name: Advanced Calculus
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Extends elementary calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations, including complex‑valued functions. Uses computer algebra software to deepen analytical skills for science and data analysis applications.
coursesExamined.contribution: extends calculus to several variables, differential equations and complex functions for analysing models of coupled living processes
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Extends elementary calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations, including complex‑valued functions. Uses computer algebra software to deepen analytical skills for science and data analysis applications.

coursesExamined.name: Linear Systems
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Analyzes continuous- and discrete-time signals and linear time-invariant systems through differential or difference equations, impulse responses and frequency-domain representations. Convolution, Fourier series and transforms lead into sampling and reconstruction, filtering, communication systems, Laplace and Z-transforms, and linear feedback. Mathematica laboratories and an applied project connect mathematical properties to signal processing and system behaviour.
coursesExamined.contribution: Actual continuous/discrete signals,convolution,Fourierseries/transforms,filtering,sampling,Laplace/Z-transforms andlinearfeedback supply mathematical analysis methods for dynamic living-system models. No unsupportedstate-space/transfer-function syllabus or molecularbiophysics equivalence asserted.
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Linear Systems studies signals and linear time-invariant systems. Students examine impulse and frequency responses, convolution, Fourier series and transforms, and the Laplace and Z transforms, including continuous-time and discrete-time representations.

coursesExamined.name: Probability & Statistics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Provides a rigorous introduction to probability and mathematical statistics, from probability spaces and random variables to multivariate distributions and statistical inference. Students study estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and maximum-likelihood methods, followed by an introduction to Bayesian reasoning. Mathematica simulations verify analytical results. A substantial project implements and compares random-sampling algorithms, including inverse sampling, accept-reject sampling and Gibbs sampling.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops probability, parameter estimation and simulation for biological measurements and model uncertainty
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics. Covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; uses computer algebra software to develop theoretical understanding and practical skills.

coursesExamined.name: Functional Anatomy
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies human anatomical structure in relation to function through regional and body-system blocks. Skeletal, thoracic, cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, reproductive and lower urinary anatomy are developed through spatial reasoning, medical images, anatomical drawing and human-specimen material. Guided practicals and dissection-room observation connect three-dimensional relationships to variation. Historical, ethical and societal questions about human remains, representation and sex accompany the anatomical study; activities are framed as academic learning rather than clinical qualification.
coursesExamined.contribution: studies anatomy through imaging/dissection and structure/function relationships, locating the consequences of cellular disease processes within functioning human systems; it is complementary anatomy rather than nanoscale imaging
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Studies human anatomical structure in relation to function through regional and body-system blocks. Medical images, anatomical drawing, human-specimen material and guided practicals develop spatial reasoning, including observation in a dissection room. Historical, ethical and societal questions accompany these academic learning activities, which do not provide clinical qualification.

coursesExamined.name: Pharmacology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies how drugs act at molecular, cellular and whole-body levels and how the body handles them. Pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, metabolism, toxicity and pharmacogenomics provide foundations for rational therapies and drug-target identification. Applications emphasize nervous-system drugs, antimicrobial treatment and inflammatory, immune and airway conditions. Quantitative exercises and virtual experiments model drug responses, while a psychoactive-drug project proposes a testable follow-up experiment.
coursesExamined.contribution: studies drug targets, interactions and kinetics, directly connecting molecular processes with therapeutic effects and toxicity
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Covers the science of drugs—their origin, composition, kinetics, therapeutic use and toxicity. Discusses drug targets, interactions and kinetics, enabling students to explain therapies in terms of molecular targets and physiological consequences.

coursesExamined.name: Infection & Immunity
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines host-microbe interactions and the immune mechanisms that protect against infection or cause disease. Microbiology and innate defence lead into antibodies, antigen recognition, lymphocyte development and memory, effector responses and mucosal immunity. Vaccination, allergy, immunodeficiency and autoimmunity connect mechanisms to clinical problems. Students analyze lymphocyte phenotypes using original flow-cytometry data and synthesize recent research in an extended and graphical abstract.
coursesExamined.contribution: studies immune recognition, receptor development, host-pathogen interactions and immunopathology as molecular/cellular mechanisms of health and disease
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Explores fundamental processes in immunology such as recognition of self vs non‑self, lymphocyte receptor development and innate and adaptive immune responses. Examines host‑pathogen interactions, inflammation, tissue damage and immunopathology.

coursesExamined.name: Mechanisms of Disease
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Connects normal organ function to pathophysiology across digestive, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, endocrine and nervous systems. Students integrate anatomy and physiology to explain symptoms, disease mechanisms, diagnostic findings, treatment and prognosis. Published clinical cases develop differential reasoning and appraisal of diagnostic procedures. A creative assignment constructs an imaginary disease whose symptoms, mechanism and proposed treatment must form a coherent pathophysiological account.
coursesExamined.contribution: Specific complementary organ/system pathophysiology connects normalfunction,causalmechanisms,diagnosticreasoning andtreatment. Publishedclinicalcases andcoherentimaginary-disease assignment develop medical-researchreasoning; not relabelled as a dedicatedmolecular/genetic-defect course.
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Examines how normal organ-system function relates to disease. Students connect anatomy and physiology with symptoms, disease mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment and prognosis across digestive, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, endocrine and nervous systems. Clinical cases and an imaginary-disease assignment develop coherent pathophysiological explanations.

coursesExamined.name: Neurobiology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies nervous systems and behaviour from comparative, evolutionary and physiological perspectives. Brain anatomy and laboratory introductions support analysis of animal behaviour, research models and welfare. The second part connects regulatory behaviour and biological rhythms to sleep, lifestyle drugs, mood and eating disorders. Comparative-anatomy work and a literature-based disorder report apply neurobiological concepts while animal-research assignments examine reduction, refinement and replacement.
coursesExamined.contribution: studies brain regions and rhythms, evolutionary complexity and research ethics, providing substantive biological content for the selected neuroscience direction
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Neurobiology studies nervous systems and behaviour through comparative anatomy, evolution and physiology. Students examine animal behaviour, research models, welfare and research ethics, then connect biological rhythms and regulatory behaviour to sleep, lifestyle drugs, mood and eating disorders. Comparative-anatomy work and a literature-based report apply neurobiological concepts.

coursesExamined.name: Perception & Action
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
coursesExamined.contribution: studies neural processing of sensory information and goal-directed action through neuroscience methods, complementing the selected computational-neuroscience direction with biological function
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.

coursesExamined.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces the molecular and cellular foundations of life and biomedical science. Students study biological molecules, cells and membranes, communication, enzymes and energy metabolism, cell division, DNA and heredity, gene expression, genomes and biotechnology. Scientific experiments and papers are analyzed through short teaching contributions and a research-based mini-symposium. A responsive final component selects additional life- and biomedical-science topics with the class.
coursesExamined.contribution: introduces macromolecules, DNA, cells and organ systems, establishing the biological foundation for molecular/quantitative investigation
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Introduces the molecular and cellular foundations of life and biomedical science. Topics include biological molecules, cells and membranes, communication, metabolism, cell division, heredity, gene expression and biotechnology. Students analyse scientific experiments and papers through teaching contributions and a research-based mini-symposium, with additional topics selected with the class.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of behaviour and mental processes. Students study neural signalling, brain anatomy and development, learning, intelligence, personality, social influence, mental disorders and treatments. Several sessions introduce behavioural, imaging and electrophysiological approaches to neuroscience and their combined use. Interdisciplinary research-article and case analysis connects psychological processes to neural mechanisms and clinical questions.
coursesExamined.contribution: introduces brain anatomy, brain injury and mental processes as the formal foundation for advanced neural perception/action study
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.

coursesExamined.name: Molecular Cell Biology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies the molecular mechanisms underlying cellular structure, physiology and regulation, primarily in eukaryotes. Bioenergetics, proteins and membranes connect to genome replication, repair and gene expression, followed by trafficking, signalling, division, tissues, stem cells and cancer. Students evaluate research methods and reproducibility and investigate a drug's molecular target, therapeutic action, metabolism and adverse effects through primary literature, a paper and a research poster.
coursesExamined.contribution: Actual eukaryoticcellstructure/regulation,bioenergetics,membranes,genome/geneexpression,trafficking/signalling/division andcancer providedirectmolecular/cellbiology. Researchmethods/reproducibility anddrug-targetprimaryliterature paper/poster are substantive; no inventedlabmodernisation activity.
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Provides foundation for practical applications in life science. Focuses on cellular biology of eukaryotes and prokaryotes, revisits concepts from introductory courses, examines current research and encourages evaluating reproducibility and modernising methods.

coursesExamined.name: Human Physiology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies normal function and regulation in the adult human body, linking molecular and cellular processes to integrated organ systems. Homeostasis, signalling and energy handling frame nervous, endocrine, muscular, respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, digestive and reproductive functions. Medical examples illustrate physiological principles. An individual literature-based paper examines a selected physiological or pathophysiological process and is developed through structured peer review and revision.
coursesExamined.contribution: studies energy handling, homeostasis, signalling and structure/function across organ systems, connecting cellular processes with their organism-level function
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Studies normal functioning of the human body, covering structure‑function relationships, energy handling, homeostasis, signalling, organ systems and integration of their functions.

coursesExamined.name: Biochemistry
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines the chemistry of life, emphasizing biomolecular structure and function, enzymes and metabolic pathways. Students study proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, enzyme kinetics and regulation, glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, the citric-acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation and further carbohydrate, lipid and nitrogen metabolism. Protein-biochemistry techniques are discussed. A literature-based disease project links a biochemical defect to symptoms, diagnostics and treatment, keeping the molecular mechanism central.
coursesExamined.contribution: studies biomolecule chemistry and metabolic pathways, directly implementing biochemistry and structure/function inquiry
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Explores the chemistry of life and biomolecules such as proteins, sugars, lipids and nucleic acids. Discusses metabolic pathways, the role of biomolecules in health and disease and applications in medicine, biotechnology and sustainability.

coursesExamined.name: Life Science Laboratory
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Provides hands-on training in biochemical, microbiological and molecular laboratory methods. Blood analysis, microbial culture and hygiene lead into bacterial transformation, green fluorescent protein production and purification, DNA isolation and analysis, and introductory bioinformatics. Students follow and sometimes adapt protocols, interpret experimental results, maintain reproducible laboratory records and communicate findings in scientific reports and figures.
coursesExamined.contribution: Actual biochemical/microbiology/molecularwetlab: bloodanalysis,microbialculture,transformation,GFPproduction/purification,DNAisolation/analysis andintroductorybioinformatics. Protocoladaptation,reproducible records andscientificreports provide realexperimentaltraining,without nanoscalebiophysicalinstrumentation.
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Introduces biochemical and molecular laboratory work. Covers themes like blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics and provides a foundation for clinical and biomedical research.

coursesExamined.name: Molecular Pathology & Genetics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Connects cellular pathology with the genetic mechanisms of human disease. Students examine injury and death, inflammation and repair, neoplasia and lymphoid malignancies, then inheritance, genetic variation, epigenetics, molecular diagnosis and genetic treatment. Ethical, legal and safety questions accompany genetic technologies. A two-year research-grant proposal integrates literature, hypotheses, method selection, controls, feasibility and budgeting; an ethics debate examines stakeholder positions.
coursesExamined.contribution: studies genetic mutations/testing, cell injury, inflammation, repair and neoplasia, directly connecting molecular/cellular structure with malfunction; it is not the full external developmental-biology or molecular-genetics syllabus
coursesExamined.preservedDescription: Covers general and molecular pathology and genetics. Studies cell injury, death, inflammation, immunity, tissue repair, regeneration, fibrosis and neoplasia, examines genetic mutations and diseases, and discusses genetic testing and ethical considerations.

physicsCandidateEvidence.ENSGATE101: Uses planetary boundaries to introduce scientific tools for understanding sustainability and human impacts on Earth systems. Students interpret graphs and uncertainty, build simple dynamic models, and learn chemical, thermodynamic and mechanical principles relevant to environmental processes. Topics connect climate, ocean acidification, nutrient cycles, energy and materials. An iterative laboratory project makes starch-based biopolymers and measures their strength and elasticity to improve the formulation.
physicsCandidateEvidence.ENSGATE201: Connects wave physics, chemistry and materials science to sustainability questions. Students study wave behaviour and observation methods, chemical analysis, microscopic material structure and macroscopic stress and strain. Practical sessions include wave applications and chemistry laboratory work. Reflective inquiries and a final project critically assess sustainability campaigns, identify greenwashing and communicate evidence-based improvements to a public audience.
